title: Deployment-tier IAM patterns and evidence matrix
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc captures recommended role patterns, policy templates, and the evidence collection matrix for each deployment tier (hosted, dedicated, private). It is intended for engineering/product/security stakeholders designing RBAC v2 mappings and the automation that feeds our SIEM and evidence store. Not final — pragmatic, testable guidance for the next sprint.

Principles and constraints (short):
- Least privilege by default; safe, auditable exceptions.
- Separate control plane (Redwood console) from data-plane compute (inference hosts).
- Role journeys (what a person does day-to-day) drive coarse roles; granular policies attached to role bindings.
- Short-lived elevation (ephemeral tokens, break-glass flows) for emergency ops.
- Strong cryptographic key controls for private deployments (KMS/HSM integration).
- All privilege changes emit structured audit events mapped to SIEM fields below.

Role families (logical):
1) Viewer (read-only): console dashboards, logs, model catalog browse, billing read access.
2) Dev (developer): deploy/test models to non-prod, create routes, read telemetry.
3) SRE (ops): scale capacity, manage node pools, restart tasks, access runtime logs.
4) Platform Admin: manage model catalog, create model versions, rollout policies.
5) Security Auditor: read-only access to audit logs, access evidence exports, run compliance reports.
6) Break-Glass Admin (emergency): full control for incident response; access gated and requires multi-party approval + automatic rotation.
7) Service Account / Workload: machine identities with narrowly scoped token permissions (e.g., embeddings-only, reranking-only).

Environment-specific guidance:
A) Hosted (Redwood multi-tenant hosted API)
- Default: customers have tenant-scoped roles (customer-admin, customer-dev, customer-viewer).
- Internals: platform roles are partitioned: platform-sre, platform-deploy, platform-observability.
- Data access: customer data is isolated; internal roles require explicit data-access grants per-tenant.
- Evidence: bind tenant-id and requestor-email into every audit event.
- Break-glass: disabled by default for hosted customer resources; any emergency access requires logged JIT request via escalation flow, 2-approver webhook, and auto-rotation.

B) Dedicated (reserved capacity for a single customer)
- Deployment model: single-tenant GPU pools in shared Redwood account or customer-managed infra depending on contract.
- Roles: dedicated-ops, dedicated-admin, dedicated-readonly. Dedicated-admin can manage pool config but cannot access customer plaintext data unless explicitly granted.
- Key handling: if KMS keys are customer-managed, any IAM policy that references KMS must include kms:Decrypt and be audited.
- Evidence: automated snapshot of config and role-bindings at every commit to infra-as-code repo recorded in evidence-store.

C) Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Deployment constraints: control-plane interactions are proxied via a customer-managed control plane or offline sync.
- Access model: keep roles minimal on Redwood control plane; prefer customer IdP for all access to data-plane.
- HSM integration: require HSM-backed signing for production model keys; any policy granting key unwrap requires explicit justification and 2 approvers.
- Evidence: collect signed attestations from on-prem agent and push timestamped manifests to secure evidence-bucket.

Role matrix (summary view - each cell is a binding guidance):
- Viewer: hosted(tenant-read), dedicated(tenant-read), private(idp-read-only)
- Dev: hosted(tenant-dev-nonprod), dedicated(tenant-dev-limited), private(dev-bridge-only)
- SRE: hosted(platform-sre-nonprod), dedicated(dedicated-ops), private(sre-bridge+customer-approved)
- Platform Admin: hosted(platform-admin-restricted), dedicated(dedicated-admin), private(minimal)
- Security Auditor: hosted(audit-read), dedicated(audit-read), private(audit-with-customer-approval)
- Break-Glass: hosted(rare/disabled), dedicated(timeboxed), private(customer-controlled)

Policy template examples (human-readable snippets):
- Minimal model-read policy (for Viewer):
  "Effect: Allow; Actions: [model.catalog.list, model.version.get]; Resource: arn:redwood:catalog:${tenant_id}:*"
- Scoped inference invoke (service account):
  "Effect: Allow; Actions: [inference.invoke]; Resource: arn:redwood:inference:${tenant_id}:routes/${route_id}; Condition: NumericLessThanEquals(session:max_tokens, 2048)"
- KMS-wrapped model key access (explicit justification required):
  "Effect: Allow; Actions: [kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey]; Resource: arn:aws:kms:region:acct:key/${key_id}; Condition: StringEquals(request:JustificationTicket, 'KMS-ACCESS-REQ-<id>')"

Break-glass / ephemeral elevation flow (recommended):
1) User requests elevation via console -> creates a JIRA ticket or emits a signed request to escalation-service.
2) Two approvers (from SRE and Security) must electronically sign policy grant.
3) System issues ephemeral token (15–60 minutes) with scope, stores the grant and the approver signatures in evidence-store.
4) All use of token logs additional fields for post-mortem.
5) Token automatically revoked; any extension re-triggers approval flow.

Evidence automation matrix (what we capture automatically):
- Event type: role_binding_change -> fields: actor_email, actor_idp, role, target_resource, timestamp, change_delta, justification_ticket.
- Event type: model_deploy -> fields: actor_email, model_id, image_digest, infra_commit_sha, region, audit_token_id.
- Event type: kms_key_use -> fields: actor_email, key_id, operation, purpose_tag, request_ticket.
- Event type: break_glass_issue -> fields: requestor, approvers[], start_ts, end_ts, token_id, actions_performed.

SIEM export schema mapping (suggested canonical fields):
- common: event_id, event_time, event_type, tenant_id, principal, principal_type, request_ip, user_agent, trace_id
- rbac: prev_role, new_role, binding_id, change_source (api/console/automation)
- workload: model_id, route_id, invocation_id, token_ttl_seconds, latency_ms, compute_region
- crypto: kms_key_id, key_usage, key_origin (customer-redwood), hsm_present
- provenance: git_commit, ci_job, deploy_manifest_hash

Mapping notes: ensure every audit event includes trace_id (correlates across logs, traces, and evidence objects) and a short schema_version field. SIEM ingestion expects newline-delimited JSON with those canonical fields.

Evidence retention and exports:
- Hosted: evidence retention default 365 days (configurable by enterprise contract). Exports to SIEM are pushed to customer-owned ingestion endpoints or to SOC team endpoints.
- Dedicated: retain infra config snapshots and role bindings for contract period + 180 days.
- Private: retention controlled by customer; Redwood stores only control-plane attestations as per contract.

Operational checklist for implementation (MVP):
- Build RBAC v2 binding API that emits structured role_binding_change events.
- Add trace_id prop to all control-plane requests and event emissions.
- Implement ephemeral token lifecycle service with approval hooks and signed evidence artifacts.
- SIEM exporter: map internal event fields to canonical schema and batch-publish via secure channel (TLS + mutual auth).
- Evidence-store: immutable bucket with object metadata: created_by, sha256, trace_id, schema_version.

Testing & validation plan:
- Unit tests for policy enforcement paths (positive and negative tests).
- Simulated break-glass: end-to-end approval, token issuance, action log verification, automatic revocation.
- Pen-tests focused on privilege escalation vectors: role impersonation, stale role bindings, token reuse.
- SIEM ingest test harness that validates schema and rejects malformed events.

Open questions / decisions for next sprint:
- What minimum TTL for ephemeral tokens balances safety vs ops friction? (15m, 30m, 60m tradeoffs)
- Should we permit limited ad-hoc access for hosted customer support during incidents, or always require explicit tenant grant?
- How do we represent multi-tenant cross-customer operations (support tools that read multiple tenants) in the RBAC model?

Action items:
- Security to propose final SIEM field whitelist and schema_version (owner: Nina Park, due: 2026-03-10).
- Infra to prototype role_binding_change event and evidence-store metadata (owner: Samir Patel, due: 2026-03-17).
- Product to review customer contract templates and update retention clauses for dedicated evidence (owner: Priya Desai, due: 2026-03-24).

Appendix: quick references
- Escalation-service whitelist: documented in CONFLUENCE-SEC/4682.
- Example infra commit link: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/abc123...
- SIEM ingestion endpoint template: https://siem-ingest.redwood.internal/push

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep templates minimal and concrete; avoid free-text justification where possible — prefer ticket ids.
- Make evidence artifacts machine-verifiable (signed metadata + sha).
- Consider a separate "auditor-only" service account for scheduled compliance exports so we avoid mixing human creds with automation.
